objects.name: Antares Descent Stage
objects.description: Lower half of Lunar Module Antares. After a tense manual landing following a computer abort signal, Shepard and Mitchell touched down at Fra Mauro — the original target for the ill-fated Apollo 13.

objects.name: American Flag
objects.description: Planted during EVA-1 near the Lunar Module. Shepard, America's first man in space, was now the oldest person to walk on the Moon at age 47.

objects.name: ALSEP Central Station
objects.description: Apollo 14's experiment package included an active seismometer, a charged particle detector, and a cold cathode ion gauge. Powered by a plutonium RTG, it operated until 1977.

objects.name: Laser Ranging Retroreflector
objects.description: An array of 100 fused-silica corner cubes, identical to the Apollo 11 unit. Still operational today — Earth-based observatories bounce laser pulses off it to measure the Earth-Moon distance with millimetre precision.

objects.name: MET (Modular Equipment Transporter)
objects.description: Nicknamed the 'lunar rickshaw,' this two-wheeled hand cart carried tools, cameras, and sample bags during the EVAs. It was the only wheeled vehicle used before the Lunar Roving Vehicle of Apollo 15.

objects.name: Shepard's Golf Balls
objects.description: Alan Shepard attached a 6-iron head to a sample tool handle and hit two golf balls on live TV, famously claiming one went 'miles and miles.' Analysis later estimated about 40 yards. The balls are still out there.

_note: Equipment positions approximate, based on Apollo 14 traverse maps. Golf ball position is estimated from TV footage.
